examples.name: Default
examples.summary: Default surface with title, description, and a trailing action.

examples.name: Outline
examples.summary: Outlined variant with a visible border.

examples.name: Muted
examples.summary: Muted variant for secondary list rows.

examples.name: Small
examples.summary: Compact density with reduced padding and gap.

examples.name: WithIconMedia
examples.summary: ItemMedia with kind icon frames a leading icon before title and description.

examples.name: WithAvatar
examples.summary: Default ItemMedia slot fits Avatar for profile-style rows.

examples.name: WithImageMedia
examples.summary: ItemMedia with kind image crops a thumbnail; a second ItemContent column can show metadata.

examples.name: WithLink
examples.summary: With href, the whole row renders as an anchor: the single focusable element of the row, with row-level hover and the focus-visible ring. Tab to a row to see it.

examples.name: WithGroup
examples.summary: ItemGroup is the off-card list: it stacks rows with a gap between them (no dividers) and forces its items inline (no per-item surface/padding) to avoid a box-in-box effect.

examples.name: WithList
examples.summary: ItemList is the in-card list: placed inside a Card with padded=false, rows are separated by full-width dividers and sit flush to the card edges.

examples.name: WithListLinks
examples.summary: Link rows inside an ItemList: each whole row is an anchor set by href (data-kind forced to default by the list), separated by full-width dividers, with row-level hover and a focus-visible ring on Tab.

examples.name: Inline
examples.summary: kind="inline" removes the outer padding so items sit flush; placed in a gapped ItemGroup directly on the page (no card, no dividers).

examples.name: Option
examples.summary: `kind="option"` rows under a search field: the 38 px chooser row of a create flow (a workload, a host). Each row is a `clickable` Item, so the row is a native button; the pressed one fills with the selected surface and shows a check. The kind sets its own density, so `size` does not change it.
